question: Once spending on a project passes the budget its owner set, what happens to their appetite for further worthwhile spending?
options: They escalate, to rescue the money
They refuse, even when it would pay
They judge only the future returns
answer: They refuse, even when it would pay. Chip Heath found people track spending against a mental budget: below it, sunk costs pull them onward; once it is exceeded, they turn down investments with good prospects. Both errors look backwards at money already gone. A house left one roof short is the same mistake, inverted.
move: Past spending is a bad reason to stop as well as to continue.
trap: Assuming sunk costs can only ever push people to keep going.
source: Heath, Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 1995
reference: Heath, Escalation and de-escalation of commitment in response to sunk costs: the role of budgeting in mental accounting, Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 1995
